finding.claim: With default configuration (allow_unsafe_links=true), javascript:/vbscript:/file:/data: link destinations are emitted into href unchanged, giving XSS to anyone who can submit Markdown. Documented default, but a real XSS for consumers who keep defaults.
finding.source: Markdown link destination, e.g. [x](javascript:alert(document.cookie)), from any untrusted Markdown author (comment or wiki field)

trace.note: forbidUnsafeLinks = !allow_unsafe_links, which is false by default
RegexHelper::isLinkPotentiallyUnsafe check is skipped when forbidUnsafeLinks is false
href set to the raw URL
Same bypass for {href=...} attributes when allow_unsafe_links is true

finding.guards_checked: RegexHelper.php:251-259 protocol check is sound (strips tab/LF/CR and leading C0 controls; entity-encoded schemes are decoded before render), but it only runs when allow_unsafe_links=false, which is not the default. Xml::escape prevents attribute breakout, not script URLs. Upstream documents the default, so this is by-design but unsafe for untrusted input.

finding.claim: Embed HTML fetched from a remote provider is emitted raw, bypassing the html_input=escape/strip setting. Plausible XSS when the embed library returns attacker-influenced HTML. NOT VERIFIED: the embed/embed library is not vendored in this repo.
finding.source: Standalone https:// line in untrusted Markdown; the attacker controls the fetched page's metadata, or any page on a domain permitted by allowed_domains

trace.note: Requires line to begin with https:// and be a standalone link
Raw HTML returned; html_input is never consulted
Contrast: raw HTML elsewhere honors html_input

finding.guards_checked: html_input is honored by HtmlBlockRenderer and HtmlInlineRenderer but not by EmbedRenderer. DomainFilteringAdapter (opt-in, EmbedExtension.php:38-41) limits hosts but uses a suffix match (DomainFilteringAdapter.php:55), so subdomains of an allowed parent such as *.github.io pass. Whether code->html can carry script depends on the unvendored library.

finding.claim: With allowed_domains left at its default of empty, any https:// URL on its own line in untrusted Markdown is fetched server-side with no private-address, redirect, or DNS-rebinding checks. Impact is limited to HTTPS destinations; the fetched HTML may be echoed back via F2.
finding.source: Standalone https:// line in untrusted Markdown (any commenter)
finding.sink: Server-side HTTP fetch by adapter->updateEmbeds during DocumentParsedEvent (EmbedProcessor.php:55)

trace.note: Domain filter only wrapped when allowed_domains is non-empty
Only the https:// prefix is required
Fetch triggered for each top-level embed
getMulti fetches each URL with no network-address filtering in this repo

finding.guards_checked: Only the https:// prefix and top-level-only placement (EmbedProcessor.php:45-50) limit requests. http:// is not reachable through this path. No private-IP, metadata-address, redirect, or DNS-pinning checks exist in this repo, and the outcome depends on the unvendored embed library's own protections, which I could not verify.
